column4: M: Part of any software project completion is a User Acceptance Test, done independently. | F: Not by the A.I. that built it? | M: No. By a qualified, C.T.F.L. certified company. Audited, and signed.

column3: M: The U.A.T. Guide. One button prints it.
column4: F: So what do the testers follow? | M: The U.A.T. Guide. Each step says what to do, and what to confirm on screen, with a box to tick. One button prints it.

column3: M: It prints as a plain document.
column4: M: It prints as a plain document. One chapter starts on a new page, every table is ruled, and every picture is labelled.

column3: M: Check the first page first.
column4: F: And this is a saved copy? | M: Yes, twenty-two pages. Check the first page before anything else: what you need, and who does which chapter.

column3: M: Chapter B uses your own Shed drawings.
column4: M: Chapter B uses your own Shed drawings. First the floor plan on its own, labelled, so the tester knows it is their building.

column3: M: Do. Confirm. Then tick, by hand.
column4: M: Every step has three parts. Do. Confirm on screen. Then tick pass, or fail, by hand.

column2: saved PDF notes line + known limits
column3: M: Write differences on the notes line.
column4: F: What if something differs? | M: Write it on the notes line. And read the known limits. Do not fail a step on something that is not built yet.

column3: M: The last page is the sign off.
column4: M: The last page is the sign off. Tester, date, passed out of total, and a signature, for each chapter.

column3: M: Test independently, and keep the signed sheets.
column4: F: What should the company keep in mind? | M: Test independently. Use the test client, not live data. The test dates are fixed, so the colours drift with the calendar. And keep the signed sheets. They are your acceptance record.
